review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–103) and grepped for uses of its declarations. The file has no @[simp] attributes. Its declarations are the cardinality theorem, the choice-based `indexEquivOfInfinite`, a comparison lemma with `Basis.indexEquiv` proved by `rfl`, and three iff/negation theorems on `Finsupp`. Two candidates came up, and I rejected both. First, I considered making `indexEquivOfInfinite_eq_indexEquiv` a simp lemma. The only uses are in the declarations themselves and in a test client that applies `indexEquivOfInfinite` directly. Nothing there needs the rewrite, and the lemma only matters under the extra `InvariantBasisNumber` hypothesis. The rubric warns against adding simp attributes solely because an identity looks simple. Second, the iff lemmas have `Nonempty` statements as their left-hand sides and are applied explicitly with `.mp` and `.trans`. I found no sign of competing rules, unwanted expansion or a rewrite cycle. I did not run Lean, so I can't rule out simp problems in downstream files I did not inspect.
